decisions.reason: The candidate already records the same-message button and knob styling changes, while bowl measurement markings were already required before this source Event. Adding bowl lighting does not alter its state.
The lighting addition does not change the machine's beige and green color scheme; the silver finish is limited to buttons and knobs and is already represented by the control-styling Requirement.
Bowl lighting supports the existing DJ-inspired visual theme but does not change the candidate's theme, desired character, lifecycle, or scope.

The request to explore an E treatment may merely reaffirm the existing marking requirement or may soften it into an exploratory design decision. The source does not safely establish which existing marking attributes should change.
The bowl-lighting decision does not change the branded placard's wording, position, orientation, or display sides.
Although lighting may consume electrical power, the source provides no load, capacity, supply, or cooling change that necessarily modifies this Requirement.
Lighting and measurement units around the bowls do not change bowl depth, capacity, or refilling behavior.
The source decision concerns bowl lighting and control appearance, not the spout's appearance, material, or fabrication method.
Adding lighting around the bowls does not alter the dispensing path, flow behavior, dripping constraints, or beverage-preservation requirements.
The lighting addition does not change splash-control targets, speed conditions, or mitigation options.
The source does not change whisk size, material, selected design, powder compatibility, or bowl-capacity assumptions.
The bowl-lighting decision has no necessary effect on spout removability or its cleaning purpose.
